# Real-text results (generated by `python -m app.eval.realtext public`; do not edit by hand)

Source: the 217 real, anonymised CVs of datasetmaster/resumes (MIT; the other 4600 are Faker-generated and excluded). Rendered from JSON to text: the language is real, the layout is ours. Mostly developer, analyst and engineering roles, so this tests the pipeline on real language, not test-automation ranking.

| Check | result |
|---|---|
| CVs parsed without error | 217/217 |
| experience or projects section found | 217/217 (100%) |
| dated roles found (years computable) | 53/217 (24%) |
| tool names written by real people that the gazetteer recognises | 396/3186 (12%); the taxonomy covers test automation only |
| tools found in free prose that the CV's own fields also list (prose precision) | 184/204 (90%) |
| quality flags | few_skills 176, no_dated_roles 164, short_text 30 |

Tools found in prose but absent from the CV's own fields (review: true mention, or gazetteer false positive?): requests (6), postman (6), python (4), javascript (2), java (2)

Testing-related tool names real people wrote that the gazetteer does not know (candidates for data/skills_taxonomy.yaml): quality management (8), functional testing (7), manual testing (6), software testing life cycle (4), software testing / quality assurance (1), integration testing (1), acceptance testing (1), smoke testing (1), ui testing (1), sanity testing (1)
